_comment: Famous dark-sky sites, so the places you would actually travel to for a sky are typeable. Hand-authored here, the same reasoning asterisms.json documents: a name and a coordinate are facts, and no third-party file is bundled. Most are certified by DarkSky International (Reserve, Park or Sanctuary) and the rest are observatory sites too well known to leave out; the certification is recorded as prose in `note`, not as a schema, because it is context rather than data anything computes from. Coordinates are a representative point, not a boundary: these are areas, some of them thousands of square kilometres, and Bortle varies across them. The point is chosen near the usual observing spot where there is one. Timezones are IANA names so the clock is right; the Bortle figure the pages show is computed from the light-pollution model, never from this file, so nothing here can claim a darkness it does not have.
